title: Cellular and molecular neuroscience
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
prerequisites: C11, C1, C3; helpful: C5, H14.
purpose: Learn how neurons compute with electricity and chemistry: ion concentrations and the Nernst and Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz equations, the membrane as an RC circuit, passive spread and the cable equation, voltage-gated channels and the Hodgkin–Huxley model, action potential propagation and myelination, synaptic transmission and quantal release, receptors and postsynaptic potentials, synaptic integration, neuromodulation, and the molecular machinery of neurons, with simulations in Python.
primary_reading: Neuronal Dynamics by Gerstner, Kistler, Naud and Paninski (free online)

weeks.1: Ions, membranes and the Nernst equation
weeks.2: The resting potential and the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz equation
weeks.3: The membrane as an RC circuit
weeks.4: Passive spread: length constants and the cable equation
weeks.5: Voltage-gated channels and the Hodgkin–Huxley model
weeks.6: Action potentials: threshold, refractoriness and propagation
weeks.8: Synaptic transmission: release, quantal analysis and receptors
weeks.11: Molecular machinery: channels, transporters and genes
weeks.12: Channelopathies and drugs that act on neurons

blocks.deliverable: Compute equilibrium and resting potentials from ion concentrations.
Simulate the charging of a membrane in code.
Simulate an action potential with Euler steps.
Week 7 midterm; analyze supplied quantal release data.
Model summation of synaptic inputs in time and space.
Explain one disease or drug at the level of channels and synapses.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Neuron simulator: build a small, tested Python program that simulates a patch of membrane with Hodgkin–Huxley channels and a synaptic input, reproduce threshold, refractoriness and the effect of blocking a channel, and write a short report with tables of your simulations and the equations behind them.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
